chapter: Bolden and the road to New Orleans
title: Freddie Keppard on violin and Willie Cornish on baritone
summary: Ory met the young Keppard playing violin in the country and recalls Cornish playing baritone.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: It was Keppard. Oh, well, Keppard came up later. That's later. Keppard came up just by the time I did New Orleans. He used to play violin, you know. I met him out in the country with my little band. He came out there. Who was playing violin? He's Freddie Keppard.
Is that so? Yeah. Before he played the cornet, huh? Yeah. Mm-hmm.
And we were playing about three miles from them, and we sold out with no more beer, no liquor, no food to sell, and so we got off about an hour early, and we went down where he was playing.
Did he have his own little group?
Yeah. And he asked me to play with him. I played with him. How was his violin playing? We had all the karate.
I had a guy who? Keppard. Oh, nothing to write home about. Uh-huh. But he was a good boy and a trumpet.
Was it a homemade violin or a regular violin?

No, a regular violin. Yeah, we was playing a real instrument then. And he was too? We were professional. We were playing professionally then. Yeah. That's how I met Freddie. Mm-hmm. And the guy playing baritone for trombone in the band. He had no trombone, he played a baritone. You know, plays with trombone. Willie Cornish.
You mean a brass baritone horn? Yeah. Yeah. I asked him, I said, why are you playing the baritone? He said, that's the best I could do. I'd have anything else to play on.
